- [Substack: Why It’s So Difficult For Companies to Go Public: A CFO Explains the Process | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 35](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/why-its-so-difficult-for-companies-150) - 2025-11-24

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Amy Butte explains IPO preparation through NYSE and Navan, emphasizing financial controls, reproducible KPIs and capable teams. Navan provides a concrete AI-support example with later revenue growth and strong gross margins, but the interview does not establish zero hallucination risk or like-for-like labor productivity versus Amex GBT. Butte explicitly declines a profitability deadline, and the career discussion is guidance rather than a quantitative employment forecast.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Treat IPO readiness as controls, tax, systems and people work, not merely a financing event.
- Demand stable KPI definitions and acquisition integration.
- Distinguish an audit concern from proof of fraud.
- Separate observed automation, causal savings and durable competitive advantage.
- Compare labor at equal service output before inferring productivity.
- Distinguish gross margins, adjusted operating income and GAAP profitability.
- Do not manufacture a horizon when management declines to forecast one.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- IPO readiness critical-path schedule
- Budget reconciliation and control remediation
- KPI definitions and cohort comparability
- AI interaction share and gross margin
- Support staffing normalized by booking/service volume
- TAM assumptions and attainable share

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Amy Butte, then Navan CFO. Most company execution and AI performance claims belong to the guest.
- All 1403caption lines were read.
- Opening montage repeats interview claims.
- Navan name and Rule 430A are garbled in captions.
- NYSEIPOshorthand is explicitly clarified as the Archipelago merger.
- The reference to Navan listing two weeks earlier suggests recording preceded publication; no exact recording date is asserted.
- Personal health disclosure and biographical details are not investment claims.
